extracted.intended_audience: UVA faculty pursuing external funding for large or center-scale collaborative projects
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and institutional requirements for faculty seeking external funding for large, collaborative, or center-scale projects at the University of Virginia, including use of Research Development services, timelines, and limited‑submission processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target project scope / eligibility for RD services
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Development team members work directly with faculty pursuing external funding for large, collaborative projects, and center-scale efforts of strategic institutional importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services are intended for large, collaborative, or institutionally strategic center-scale efforts — smaller or individual-project proposals are not the primary focus of these services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance request timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases, services must be requested at least 3 months prior to the sponsor’s deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty should plan and request Research Development support well in advance (≈3 months) to allow for opportunity identification, proposal development, iterative reviews, and institutional processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service availability and authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Our services are available upon request and at the discretion of the Associate VP for Research Development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to Research Development support requires a formal request and is subject to approval by the Associate VP; not all requests are guaranteed to receive support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited Submission Opportunity (LSO) internal selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited Submission Opportunities (LSOs) are those in which the sponsor has placed a restriction on the number of proposals, applications, or nominations that may be submitted from an institution. The Research Development team is responsible for managing the university’s selection process for LSOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For LSOs faculty must participate in the university’s internal selection process managed by Research Development; adherence to that selection process is required before external submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of opportunity scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Development helps identify appropriately-scaled opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty should work with RD to ensure the funding opportunity matches the project's scale, scope, and institutional priorities to maximize competitiveness and alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managed proposal development and iterative review
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Development provides managing of the proposal development process, and provides advice and iterative reviews to enhance competitiveness of proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals supported by RD will be managed through stages and are expected to undergo iterative feedback cycles; applicants should be prepared to revise and incorporate RD input to improve competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of research intelligence in decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The team provides research intelligence to inform decisions relevant to the research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty and units are encouraged to use RD-supplied intelligence (e.g., funding landscapes, sponsor expectations) when choosing opportunities and shaping proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skill and sponsor-expectations development
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Development team curates and creates workshops, training events, webinars and programs designed to enhance our faculty’s grant-getting skills and increase awareness of sponsor expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty should engage with RD training and resources to improve grant-writing skills and to better understand funder requirements and norms; these programs are part of RD's support ecosystem.
